Hello! I'm Aurora & I'm just getting into Lean, I'm liking it a lot as far!

There is one thing I've come across a few times, especially when using simp or assumption, that confuses me as to what it's trying to say. I'll sometimes get stuff like simp is a flexible tactic modifying ⊢ or assumption modifies ⊢. Isn't modifying the goal the point of using these tactics?

If you refer to this page (https://leanprover-community.github.io/extras/simp.html), under non-terminal simp, it explains the issue in more detail, but basically, the result that simp produces can very easily change when mathlib gets more simp lemmas, you add simp lemmas, or you change the files you import (which changes the available simp lemmas). This means that if simp isn't the very last tactic you use to close the goal, it could eventually end up producing a different result than it did when you first wrote the proof, which could break the proof. That's why it's often better to change this so-called "non-terminal simp" to the suggestion you get when you change "simp" to "simp?", which is called squeezing the simp. (See https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html#squeezing-simp-calls)

So what the warning is telling you (somebody else correct me if this is wrong), is that the subsequent tactics after the simp you use, modify a goal that was modified by simp, and therefore your proof will likely break, if simp later produces a different result.

Two of the usual fixes: (1) replace simp with simp? and then click on the blue action in the infoview which will change it to simp only [possibly huge list] (2) run simp, look at the goal, and then write suffices <that goal> by simpa.

The linter is basically for the mathlib maintainers -- we maintain code which people who may even have left the community have written, and fixing up other people's code can be annoying so we have tools which make it hard for them to write hard-to-maintain code. If this is just for a personal project then you can just switch the linter off.
Yeah I got the simp? part & understood it's just for searching for what to use, I just didn't get the objective of the warning, but that makes sense! thanks!
